s: A company has 40 business applications, each deployed with AWS CloudFormation. Tier-1 applications must meet an RTO of 1 hour and an RPO of 15 minutes for AZ and Regional disruptions. Tier-2 applications have looser targets. The CTO wants each application measured against its tier targets after every deployment, recommendations to close any gaps, and notification when an application drifts out of compliance. The solution must have the LEAST operational overhead. Which solution meets these requirements?
o: Use AWS Resilience Hub. Create resiliency policies for each tier, import each application from its CloudFormation stacks, run an assessment from the CI/CD pipeline after each deployment, and enable drift notifications.
Use the AWS Well-Architected Tool to run a Reliability pillar review of each application every quarter and track the improvement plans.
Deploy AWS Config conformance packs that check for Multi-AZ, backup plans, and Auto Scaling, and send noncompliance to AWS Security Hub CSPM.
Use AWS Trusted Advisor fault tolerance checks and export the results weekly to Amazon S3 for analysis in Amazon Athena.

w.y: Resilience Hub assesses applications against resiliency policies that set RTO and RPO per disruption type, gives recommendations, and alerts on drift. Assessments can run from a pipeline. It is the only option that measures against RTO/RPO targets with little effort.

o.A: Correct: tiered resiliency policies, pipeline-run assessments, recommendations, and drift notifications.
o.B: Quarterly manual reviews do not run after every deployment and are labor-intensive.
o.C: Config rules check individual settings but do not estimate whether an application meets its RTO/RPO.
o.D: Trusted Advisor checks are generic and not tied to per-application RTO/RPO targets. Full checks also need a higher support plan.

d: measure against RTO/RPO targets per tier, LEAST operational overhead
